script: We began with the people moving a home forward, not an agent for every department. Nine company-role research instruments contributed to desk research. The atlas covers 28 stage-based maps and 24 bounded opportunities.

Across the eight-stage journey, three hypotheses recur: people repeat their story, a sent promise has no accepted receiver, and a changed scope leaves a review stale. The design response is one case, a named receiving owner, and separate decisions whose dependencies can be checked.

These maps informed the design; they are not direct resident or staff research. The next test is whether real people can complete these tasks, including assisted routes, without transferring effort or weakening choice.
slides.diagram: Eight connected, numbered native chevrons: 1 report or nominate -> 2 understand home and household -> 3 decide scope and feasibility -> 4 coordinate ready work -> 5 deliver and capture -> 6 inspect and remedy -> 7 handover and live with measures -> 8 reconcile and learn. Stage-linked pain hypotheses: 1-2 repeated story, test one sourced case and safe sharing; 4 unowned promises, test a named receiver with sender chase until accepted; 3 and 6 stale reviews, test separate version-bound decisions and reopen affected reviews. Arrows attach these hypotheses below the relevant journey stages; words and numbers carry the meaning without colour.
caveats: The 27 companion maps plus the atlas leasehold-service staff map make 28 stage-based maps; two added subjourneys are not silently counted as additional maps.
All pain and gain statements are hypotheses or desired outcomes, not measured emotion scores, quotations, customer endorsement or delivered gains.

slides.subject: The same-home service blueprint

headers.text: One home, end to end: every exception has an owner.

elements.text: Fictional service synthesis: a proposed experience, not an actual system trace or delivered-feature claim
CHANGE EXCEPTION   Changed scope -> named receiver -> affected reviews reopen -> resident update
Hazards use an independent human route. Access, silence or a booking never implies works consent.

script: Follow the same fictional home across five moments, with the resident, delivery team and Finance plus QA visible together. This is a service blueprint synthesised from research, not an actual system trace or a claim that every feature is delivered.

The resident can agree, defer or decline specific works. Delivery accepts competent capacity, not merely an offered date. Independent QA can return work; resident handover does not settle a claim or create cash.

When scope changes, the exception has a named receiver. Only dependent reviews reopen, with a separate resident update. Hazard intake never waits for the retrofit workflow, and a survey visit or booking is never inferred works consent.
slides.diagram: Five columns: report/understand; choose scope; book/deliver; inspect/handover; claim/reconcile. Three lanes: resident choice and aftercare; delivery evidence, design, capacity and remedy; Finance and independent QA route, affordability, inspection and cash. At scope choice Finance owns budget and the resident owns works choice; independent QA accepts or returns at inspection. Amber cells explicitly labelled CHANGE mark scope review reopening and commitment-version rechecking; the CHANGE EXCEPTION rail names the receiver, reopens affected reviews and updates the resident. Hazard intake stays a parallel independent human route. Labels, not colour alone, identify the exception.
caveats: Fictional synthesis, not a customer observation, live transaction trace, delivered-feature checklist or measured outcome.
Finance and QA share a drawing lane, not a decision authority: professional review, resident consent, Finance approval, independent QA, handover and financial closure remain separate.
Phone, letter, visits and assisted service remain usable; no portal is required. Hazards, withdrawal, safeguarding and redress do not wait for the sequential rail.

script: The latest delivery lesson is the draft paper Everything But the Software, with author clarification dated 25 October 2026. The 'Before and during the delivery loop' table records 183 merged pull requests over 15-24 October and 36,755 words appended to the knowledge-base log over 15-22 October. This is an exploratory single case with rival explanations, not causal proof that agents degrade software. It challenges counting output as usable delivery. My proposed feedback rail is feature, tests, use journey, then keep, cut or tidy before adding more.

The research question is whether an additional agent can perform bounded reflection and course correction, not whether reflection is exclusively human. The selected S1 comparison is four runs per arm, ten features and full CR1. The proposed consolidation experiment is paused, registration is pending and there are no study results. script: The plain answer is no: this design has not been validated through direct resident or staff research. Owner feedback, prototype review and nine role instruments informed it, but none is customer endorsement.

These three representative maps expose testable hypotheses: the resident needs meaningful choice without repeating the story; the assessor needs traceable preparation and observations; the Finance preparer needs version-correct evidence and separate cash reconciliation.

The next empirical work is direct, privacy-governed task and comprehension testing with relevant residents and staff, including assisted routes, access needs, handoff failures and net effort. Desired gains stay hypotheses until that evidence exists.
